Maya,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. As part of Acme's internal readiness review we need a short checklist and evidence package showing how Redwood's private deployment will handle:

- Control-plane/data-plane separation during scale-up (pod addition + control plane leader election)
- KV cache egress controls (no unexpected outbound connections)
- Telemetry retention proof (sampling intervals, tenant-tagged traces)
- A small set of test artifacts we can run to validate in our staging colo

Can you send a one-page runbook + any sample logs/traces we can use to validate? Prefer PDF or CSV evidence attachments.

Goal: we aim to complete the acceptance gate by Feb 22, so any time this week is great.

Thanks — Samir

Samir —

Appreciate the summary. Attached is a concise runbook (runbook-vpc-scaling.md) that walks through the scaling scenario and the minimal evidence package we recommend. Highlights:

- Control plane behavior: leader election is performed inside the control-plane replica set; we hold a maintenance window for PV reattachment and stepwise reprovisioning of data-plane pods to avoid KV cache TTL storms.
- KV cache egress: all runtime containers are configured with an egress-deny policy by default; explicit egress is only allowed to internal metrics collectors and customer-approved NTP/DNS endpoints.
- Telemetry: tenant-tagged traces are sampled at 1% by default; critical path sampling can be bumped for short windows. We include example trace snippets and a CSV (kvcache-latency-samples.csv) you can inject into your trace-processor.

Attachments included: runbook-vpc-scaling.md, egress-evidence-20280216.pdf (sample audit export), kvcache-latency-samples.csv

Planned next steps:
1) Jonás (cc'd) will validate the control-plane leader-change steps against our staging cluster and provide the exact CLI sequence.
2) Naomi will produce a short list of trace IDs showing no external egress during the KV cache warm-up.
3) Kimberly will coordinate a brief run (15–30 minutes) you can trigger from your side with our test harness.

If you want, we can also do a 30-minute screenshare to walk the runbook and trace artifacts.

Best,
Maya

On Thu, Feb 16, 2028 at 10:05 AM maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai wrote:
> Attached is a concise runbook ...

Quick technical notes and exact commands you can run in staging:

- Control plane scale scenario (happy path):
  1) curl -X POST https://ops.local/api/scale -d '{"node_group":"data-plane","count":+3}' — this triggers the orchestration controller to allocate new data-plane pods with pre-warmed KV caches.
  2) We perform cordon & drain with pod-propagated leader pinning to avoid concurrent re-elections for critical controllers.
  3) After pods report Ready, run: ./tools/validate-connectivity --mode egress-check --allowed endpoints.json to assert no outbound connections beyond allowed set.

- Egress verification: we provide the sample egress-audit policy (attached PDF) that includes conntrack summaries and SDN flow dumps. The key check is that during warm-up we observe only connections to 10.0.0.0/8 and the internal metrics collector (10.90.77.14). Any deviation is a fail.

- KV cache specifics: cache warm-up will produce slightly elevated latency (see kvcache-latency-samples.csv). We intentionally cap background fetch parallelism to 8 to avoid excessive external fetches.

Action items for Acme:
- Run the egress-check tool above from a jump host and share the raw flow dump.
- If possible, grant temporary visibility to our audit collector (read-only) so Naomi can pull the short trace samples we referenced.

I'll follow up with exact CLI snippets in a Gist if that helps.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
